solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aristocrat and king in outstanding environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so the king sits within the word for outstanding

blocks.note: outstanding as a debt still owed is due
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a monarch stand together in some impressive setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent, but here it means unpaid, as a bill can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is a nobleman of the highest rank below a prince, so an aristocrat.

clue.text: Animal protecting right area of body

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap around it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a beast is an animal
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A creature guards its rights over some territory around its body.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is the front of the chest, a region of the human or animal body.

clue.text: Bikes encapsulating commercial for European archipelago

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing completely, so one word holds the other inside

blocks.note: bikes are cycles
a commercial is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: Bicycles bearing advertising promote holidays in a group of European islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cyclades are the Greek islands of the Aegean that circle Delos, including Mykonos and Santorini.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades form a large island group in the Aegean Sea belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Reserve small chilled desserts

blocks.note: ice can mean coldness of manner, reserve in a person
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An instruction to set aside some small cold puddings for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' reads as a verb meaning book; it is the noun for an aloof, cool manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are frozen sweets such as ice creams and sorbets served as dessert.

clue.text: Inspector lifted rule, overseeing one religious festival

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means turned upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top
in a down clue, overseeing places one part above the next one

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a rule is a law
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A police inspector lifts a regulation while supervising a single religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights celebrated in autumn, a major religious holiday.

clue.text: Back-to-back felines inside so disconnected

indicators.note: two things placed back to back face opposite ways, so the first pet is written backwards
inside puts the pair of animals within the short word that follows

blocks.note: felines are cats, here two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two cats sitting back to back seem detached from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Back to back, the two cats meet tail to tail: the first is written backwards against the second, and the pair goes inside SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is the musical term for notes played short and detached, each separated from the next.

clue.text: Animal hunted where excavations are carried out

blocks.note: first meaning: the prey of a hunter
second meaning: a pit where stone is dug out

explanation.surface: A beast being chased into a site where digging goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the creature being pursued and an open pit from which stone is extracted.

clue.text: Companion at home finally cut variable cotton fabric

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: CH is a Companion of Honour
someone at home is in
the last letter of cut
Z is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A housemate at last trims some patterned cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton cloth, usually with floral patterns, used for curtains and furniture.

clue.text: Legendary strongman runs through Chelsea, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of the place name are set out oddly
running through something means passing inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
R is runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A mythical muscleman jogs oddly through the London district of Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles is the Greek name of Hercules, the hero of myth famed for his strength and twelve labours.

clue.text: Artist recalled church's curved structure

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word comes backwards

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A painter remembered the curving design of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved span over an opening, a classic curved building element.

clue.text: After, newsman wrote on social media

blocks.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
ED is short for editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: Later on, a journalist put something up online.
explanation.definitionFit: To post is to publish a message online, so posted is the past tense of writing on a platform.

clue.text: Oscar, then out to lunch, meets Dorothy punctually

indicators.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, so the word beside it is scrambled

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
Dot is a pet name for Dorothy

explanation.surface: Oscar goes off for lunch and then meets Dorothy right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to lunch' looks like Oscar's plans for midday; it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot is an idiom for exactly at the stated time, which is being punctual.

clue.text: Vast coniferous forest where wild cat heard

indicators.note: heard means the solver goes by how the word is said, not spelt

blocks.note: a tiger is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: A huge pine forest where the cry of a wild cat can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TIGER and TAIGA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiga is the belt of coniferous forest across Siberia and northern Canada, south of the tundra.

clue.text: Bird of prey's new cry of distress south of Devon river

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of puts the later pieces beneath the river

blocks.note: the Taw is a river in Devon, in south-west England
N is the abbreviation for new
a yowl is a loud wail of pain or distress

explanation.surface: A hawk has a fresh shriek of alarm below a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny owl is a common brown European owl, which hunts small animals, so a raptor.

clue.text: Period dresser auntie displays

indicators.note: displays means shows something it carries, so the letters lie inside the phrase

blocks.note: the end of dresser and the start of auntie

explanation.surface: An aunt shows off a dresser from a historical period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period dresser' suggests antique furniture; the definition stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct span of history, a period of time.

clue.text: Spanish food tramp eats occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A vagrant now and then dines on Spanish snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes served in Spain, often with drinks.

clue.text: Place to preach sensational stuff connected to Italian

blocks.note: pulp is lurid, sensational writing, as in pulp fiction
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A preacher's platform tied in with dramatic Italian material.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the raised stand in a church from which a sermon is delivered.

clue.text: Fictional doctor and wife visiting family member

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
visiting a place is being at it
a son is a member of a family

explanation.surface: A doctor from fiction and his wife call on a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' looks like a container signal; it simply gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's companion and chronicler in Conan Doyle's stories.

clue.text: Holy believer initially thwarts robbery

indicators.note: initially keeps only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of thwarts
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A devout person at first foils a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in a god, so a person of religious faith.

clue.text: Brewed drink left for duck

blocks.note: tea is brewed
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A pot of tea is left out for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' wants to be an anagram signal; here it just describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling duck.

clue.text: Old poet excited Wilde, say

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An earlier poet got Oscar Wilde, for instance, worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilde, say' looks like Wilde as an example of an old poet, but both words are anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was a 20th-century Anglo-Irish poet and Poet Laureate, father of the actor.

clue.text: Appreciates accommodation

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for likes or enjoys
second meaning: rented lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for likes, as in he really goes for it, and British slang for a lodger's rented room.

clue.text: Plan article supporting freshwater fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the article underneath, holding up the fish

blocks.note: the ide is a European freshwater fish
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A scheme in which some item props up a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or proposal, so a plan in the sense of a scheme.

clue.text: Relatives during gentle run having a laugh

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a jog is a gentle run
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Family members on a slow jog together, sharing a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a laugh' is British idiom for not being serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking means not serious, kidding around; the idiom having a laugh means the same thing.

clue.text: Wide county, an ancient English territory

blocks.note: W is a wide in cricket scoring, a ball bowled out of reach
Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: A broad shire described as an old English region.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the West Saxons in southern England.
